problem: Full fine-tuning of large pre-trained VLN models (e.g. HAMT) for every downstream VLN task is costly in training and storage, and off-the-shelf PETL methods (BitFit, Prompt Tuning) degrade badly on VLN, which is a dynamic, history-dependent decision task.
motivation: Real robots struggle to train and store a full model copy per task, so parameter-efficient tuning matters for VLN. VLN depends on history of past actions and on cross-modal interaction between instruction and vision, which generic PETL modules do not target, especially when most weights are frozen.
key_idea: Insert VLN-specific bottleneck modules (Historical Interaction Booster and Cross-modal Interaction Booster, both cross-attention with learnable gates) plus a language-encoder adapter and LoRA into a frozen HAMT, tuning only about 2.8% of parameters.
insight: Cross-modal interaction is the most valuable place to spend tuning parameters: CIB alone gives REVERIE val-unseen SPL 21.62 versus 18.21 (LEA alone) and 18.49 (HIB alone), and beats the plain adapter counterpart CEA (SPL 21.62 vs 20.77, RGSPL 12.86 vs 10.14). The components are complementary (LEA+HIB+CIB 26.51 SPL, adding LoRA 27.67), and a learnable gate beats a fixed alpha=0.5 (RGSPL 15.96 vs 14.50). Prompt Tuning and BitFit fail on VLN, especially on RxR with long instructions.
method: Baseline HAMT: frozen pre-trained two-stream model (language encoder, vision encoder with history encoding, cross-modal encoder); only injected modules and prediction heads are trained.
Language Encoder Adapter (LEA): parallel bottleneck adapters added to the self-attention and FFN layers of the language encoder, bottleneck dim 64.

Historical Interaction Booster (HIB): in vision encoder blocks, down-projects the observation feature and previous history feature, applies multi-head cross-attention (query=observation, key/value=history), mixes with a ReLU path through a learnable gate alpha=Sigmoid(theta/T), T=0.1, then up-projects and adds it to the block output with LN.

Cross-modal Interaction Booster (CIB): in cross-modal encoder blocks, applies two-stream bottleneck cross-attention (language attends to vision and vision attends to language), each with a learnable gate, then up-projects and adds residually.
LoRA: low-rank updates on the query and value matrices of all multi-head attention layers (rank 8 for REVERIE, 16 for other tasks).
Training: same RL+IL recipe as HAMT, AdamW with lr 1e-4, batch size 4 (REVERIE) or 8 (others); 4 attention heads in HIB and CIB.

setting.backbone: HAMT (pre-trained, frozen) plus trainable LEA/HIB/CIB/LoRA modules
setting.model_size: about 2.82% of HAMT parameters updated (1.67% on RxR)
setting.training_data: Downstream task data of R2R, REVERIE, NDH and RxR (English), with RL+IL as in HAMT; no extra data beyond HAMT pre-training
setting.observation: panoramic RGB image features with angle features, plus history of past panoramas and instruction (dialog for NDH)

results: VLN-PETL updates only about 2.8% of parameters yet matches or beats full fine-tuning on several metrics: R2R val-unseen SR 65.47 vs 64.24 and SPL 60.01 vs 59.25, and NDH GP better than fine-tuning on all splits (test-unseen 6.13 vs 5.05). It also consistently beats LoRA and Adapter, the strongest PETL baselines, on most metrics across R2R, REVERIE, NDH and RxR.
limitations: Evaluated only on navigation and object-grounding VLN tasks with no environment interaction (e.g. manipulation), and only with HAMT as the backbone.
On REVERIE test-unseen, LoRA is slightly better on SR/SPL; a gap to full fine-tuning remains on some metrics (REVERIE val-unseen SPL 27.67 vs 28.92).
Modules use a discrete nav-graph action space in simulation only; no real-robot validation.
